summary: At 6,237 feet of elevation, South Lake Tahoe sits on the southern shore of the largest alpine lake in North America, which means winter daily highs average well below freezing while summer afternoons rarely crack 80°F — an annual average high of just 56°F that makes air conditioning essentially irrelevant. That alpine setting delivers 9.3 hours of sunshine per day on average, but it also delivers the tradeoff that defines life here: a median home value of $630,200 against a median household income of roughly $73,900 puts the price-to-income ratio above 8.5, punishing for a local economy powered largely by tourism, hospitality, gaming (Stateline's casinos sit just across the Nevada border), and outdoor recreation rather than high-wage industries. Rents at $1,467 monthly are more digestible, but the job market is narrow — switching employers often means switching to another hotel, ski resort, or restaurant, and many positions are seasonal. The town itself is a linear sprawl along US Route 50 and Lake Tahoe Boulevard, more strip-mall corridor than walkable village, though Heavenly Mountain's gondola launches from near the commercial core and miles of lakeshore trail are minutes away. The essential tension is stark: world-class natural beauty paired with a thin, tourism-dependent economy where the median household would need to stretch dramatically to own.
